items.title: NVIDIA Advances Isaac Platform for General-Purpose Robotics With New Reference Humanoid, Frameworks, Simulation Pipelines and Data
items.snippet: NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform, adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework. Together, these technologies give developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster.

items.title: Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform
items.snippet: Coding agents — agents that manage git repos, edit files, and run tests in a development-ready sandbox, like our cloud coding agent Ramp Inspect. More than simple chat agents, these coworkers manage subagents, automations, sandboxes, cloud browsers, and MCP connectors to complete tasks that can take minutes or hours.

items.title: M-Plan: Comprehensive Planning For LLM Agents with Memory Arrangement
items.snippet: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have recently demonstrated outstanding performance in single-turn tasks, yet they continue to struggle with long-horizon tasks, particularly in environments without prior training. A key limitation of single LLMs is their difficulty in processing long contexts, which stems from weaknesses in continuous decision-making and reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
items.snippet: Build the Future of Artificial Intelligence (The paper presents a large-scale evaluation of GPT-6-Astra across 12 embodied benchmarks covering tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands, using a unified protocol with in-context learning from training demonstrations and a substantially larger execution-step budget.)

items.title: Introducing Scope: Open-source evaluation for AI coding agents
items.snippet: Introducing Scope, Microsoft's open-source platform for evaluating AI coding agents with repeatable experiments to improve developer agent experiences. The Judge service uses large language model (LLM) based evaluation to assess the output against those criteria, helping teams see which requirements were met and where further investigation is needed.

items.title: How to Build AI Agents by Augmenting LLMs with Codified Human Expert Domain Knowledge? A Software Engineering Framework
items.snippet: This paper investigates how to capture and embed human domain knowledge into AI agent systems through an industrial case study. We propose a software engineering framework to capture human domain knowledge for engineering AI agents in simulation data visualization by augmenting a Large Language Model (LLM) with a request classifier, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for code generation, codified expert rules, and visualization design principles unified in an agent demonstrating autonomous, reactive, proactive, and social behavior.

items.title: LLM-Driven Query Planning for Intelligent Access to Structured and Semi-Structured Data
items.snippet: This paper addresses intelligent access to structured and semi-structured data using large language models (LLMs). We develop an approach to... The proposed architecture separates planning from execution and allows SQL operations to be combined with semantic processing by an LLM.

items.title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
items.snippet: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions.

items.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
items.snippet: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million.

items.title: Open X Embodiment: Research, Data, and Evaluation Guide
items.snippet: Open X-Embodiment is broad in both the number of platforms represented and the range of behavior recorded. The paper describes an open dataset with more than one million real-robot trajectories across 22 embodiments. The project site describes the collection as 60 existing datasets pooled from 34 robotics research labs.

items.title: I built a containerized Multi-Agent Research Pipeline using LangGraph, Celery, and MCP
items.snippet: I built a containerized Multi-Agent Research Pipeline using LangGraph, Celery, and MCP. This system allows for scalable execution of complex multi-agent workflows, leveraging technologies like LangGraph for agent orchestration, Celery for task queuing, and MCP for inter-process communication.

items.title: Show HN: What the Harness? LLM agent inconsistencies in MCP implementation
items.snippet: We (Polytomic) noticed that LLM agents (Claude, Codex, Grok, Amp, etc) are inconsistent in their MCP implementations. We made tables inspired by the browser-compatibility tables of yore that list the differences. Hope you find this as useful as we did!

items.title: Show HN: Qwen3-4B with the AI writing tics trained out
items.snippet: A hobbyist fine-tuned Qwen3-4B-Instruct on a MacBook Air to remove telltale AI writing tics (em dashes, 'not X, but Y', lists of three, rhetorical signposting) without a system prompt. Using a distillation pipeline across three rounds, a custom slop-detector score dropped from 121 to 12.5 per 1000 words while retaining factual accuracy (30/30) and reasonable task fit (80%).

items.title: llm-d 1.0, an open source stack for distributed inference
items.snippet: llm-d 1.0 consolidates a hardened core for distributed inference validated for day 2 production deployments that helps organizations improve AI serving efficiency and scale enterprise workloads. In a published benchmark across a 17,000-node multi-region GKE deployment serving a mixture-of-experts model, llm-d scaled throughput 2.9x.
